'''Barton Zwiebach Cantor''' (born October 4, 1954) is a Peruvian [[string theory|string theorist]] and professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].

==Work==
Zwiebach was born in Peru to a Jewish family and studied [[electrical engineering]] at the [[Universidad Nacional de Ingeniería]] in Peru, graduating in 1977.<ref name="t272">{{cite web | last=Hayyim | first=Mayyim | title=An International and Multicultural Ritual Immersion | website=Mayyim Hayyim | date=2012-09-19 | url=https://www.mayyimhayyim.org/an-international-and-multicultural-ritual-immersion-2/ }}</ref><ref name="o979">{{cite web | title=Open Letter regarding growing antisemitism at MIT | url=https://docs.house.gov/meetings/ED/ED00/20231205/116625/HHRG-118-ED00-20231205-SD007.pdf | access-date=2025-07-30}}</ref> He subsequently attended graduate school in physics at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. He obtained his Ph.D. in 1983, working under the supervision of [[Murray Gell-Mann]]. He then held postdoctoral positions at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT). At MIT, he became an assistant professor of physics in 1987 and a permanent member of the faculty in 1994.<ref name="h968">{{cite web | title=Barton Zwiebach » MIT Physics | website=MIT Physics | date=2025-05-28 | url=https://physics.mit.edu/faculty/barton-zwiebach/ }}</ref>

He is one of the world's leading experts in [[string field theory]]. He wrote the textbook ''A First Course in String Theory'' (2004, {{ISBN|0-521-83143-1}}), meant for undergraduates.<ref>{{cite book|author=Barton Zwiebach|title=A First Course in String Theory|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XmsbvP1uUeIC|date=10 June 2004|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-83143-7|postscript=; 558 pages}}</ref><ref name="Gleiser2005">{{cite journal|last1=Gleiser|first1=Marcelo|authorlink=Marcelo Gleiser|title=Review of ''A First Course in String Theory A First Course in String Theory'' by Barton Zwiebach|journal=Physics Today|volume=58|issue=9|year=2005|page=57|issn=0031-9228|doi=10.1063/1.2117825|doi-access=free}}</ref>
